Tokens: the smallest
unit of a design system
By the end you will be able to name a token, decide what deserves one, and read a system's tokens to predict how it will age.
slides go up Friday. listen first, write second
The three ideas from last time
A component is a contract about behaviour, not a picture
Every variant doubles the surface you must test
The parts nobody owns are the parts that rot
How tokens make a second brand cheap
the recap is five minutes. hold your questions
What we mean by a token
Old English tacen: a sign, a mark that stands in for the thing itself.
A name with no decision behind it.
A bundle of tokens with one use.
A name for a value the system has decided on. Components use the name, never the value.
The button, the link, the focus ring
Every gap on every screen is a multiple of it
say it back in your own words first
A token is a named decision
When the value changes, every use changes with it. When the name is missing, every use is a separate decision waiting to drift.
If two designers would pick a different value, it deserves a token. If everyone would pick the same one, it does not.
A token is not a component and not a style. It is the one number or colour underneath both, named for why.
the test is the part everyone forgets
A product with a light and a dark theme. The accent must read on both, and every value gets a name.
count the values with me. there are twelve
A product with a light and a dark theme, and one accent that must read on both.
Ground, surface, ink, muted ink, accent, line. Six names, twelve values.
The button uses accent and ink-on-accent. It never mentions a hex.
Twelve values change, zero components change. That is the whole point.
step four is the whole lecture
Naming the value, not the decision
'blue-500' is a value with a name. 'accent' is a decision. The first breaks the moment the brand turns green.
Forty spacing tokens is a ruler, not a system. Six is a decision.
Every ground needs an ink that reads on it. The dark theme is where this is discovered, expensively.
I have made all three of these. Twice.
Name the decision, not the value. Everything else in a design system follows from that.
Lecture four, the one line to write down
if you write one thing down, this is it
Take any product you use daily and write its six tokens from observation alone. Bring the one you could not name.
one product, six names, no peeking at the code
